title: Projectivity and smooth frame fibres of the unpointed level normalization
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $g\geq2$ an integer and $\ell\geq3$ a prime different from $\operatorname{char}(k)$. Use the stable moduli groupoid $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0}$, its smooth open $\mathcal M_{g,0}$ and the full abelian level groupoid of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Write $L_{g,\ell}$ for its representing smooth level scheme [lem-sfb-smooth-curve-abelian-level-rigidification], $Q_g$ for the finite-type projective coarse scheme [lem-sfb-unpointed-stable-coarse-projective], and $(Z_{g,\ell},a)$ for the normalization in the full level cover, retaining all generic components, with $a:Z_{g,\ell}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0}$ [lem-sfb-stable-abelian-level-normalization].

Then $Z_{g,\ell}$ is finite type over $k$ and H-projective: there are $N\geq0$ and a closed immersion $Z_{g,\ell}\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ over $k$. The map $a$ specifies an actual stable unpointed genus-$g$ family $X\to Z_{g,\ell}$, with projectivity in the projective-bundle sense. For every field extension $F/k$ and every smooth projective geometrically connected genus-$g$ curve $C/F$, the functor on $F$-schemes $B$ of pairs $(z,\beta)$ with $z:B\to Z_{g,\ell}$ a $k$-map and $\beta:X\times_{Z_{g,\ell}}B\xrightarrow{\sim}C\times_F B$ an isomorphism over $B$, is naturally isomorphic to the frame functor $B\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}(\underline{(\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z)^{2g}}_B,\mathcal H_{C_B/B})$ of that definition. This functor is represented by a finite etale surjective $F$-scheme, including when it has no $F$-rational point.

Fields and field extensions use [def-weil-field] and [def-pc-field-extension]; schemes, finite type, H-projectivity, bundle projectivity, smoothness, finite morphisms, etaleness and fibre products use [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-pc-fibre-product].

proof.text: Write $h:Z_{g,\ell}\to Q_g$ for the finite morphism supplied by the normalization theorem. The coarse theorem makes $Q_g$ finite type over $k$. Choose its finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, with each $A_i$ finitely generated over $k$. Finiteness makes each inverse image affine $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, with $B_i$ a finite $A_i$-module. Choose module generators $b_{ij}$; these also generate $B_i$ as an $A_i$-algebra, since every element is an $A_i$-linear combination of them. Together with the finite $k$-algebra generators of $A_i$, they generate $B_i$ over $k$. These finitely many affine inverse images cover $Z_{g,\ell}$, proving finite type by the stated affine-cover definition.

proof.text: Apply the finite-over-projective theorem with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $T=Q_g$, $Y=Z_{g,\ell}$, and $h$ from Step 1. The base is affine and Noetherian: its only nonempty affine open is itself, and a field has just the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$. The coarse theorem supplies the finite-projective-space embedding of $Q_g$; it is quasi-compact because it is finite type, so it satisfies the projectivity convention required by that theorem. The affine-base conclusion therefore gives $N\geq0$ and a closed immersion $Z_{g,\ell}\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ over $k$. This is precisely H-projectivity in the item; no projectivity assertion over an arbitrary nonaffine base is used.

proof.text: Evaluate $a:Z_{g,\ell}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0}$ on the identity of $Z_{g,\ell}$. A map to this moduli groupoid is, by its current definition, an object over its domain. Thus this evaluation is an actual stable unpointed genus-$g$ family $X\to Z_{g,\ell}$ with projectivity in the projective-bundle convention. For $z:B\to Z_{g,\ell}$, apply the functor $a$ to the arrow $z\to\mathrm{id}_{Z_{g,\ell}}$ over $z$ in the represented scheme groupoid. The definition of an arrow over $z$ gives precisely an isomorphism $a(z)\xrightarrow{\sim}X\times_{Z_{g,\ell}}B$ over $B$. Composition of these arrows uses the canonical associativity isomorphism of fibre products, so these identifications commute with further base change. This identifies the family in the item and its pullbacks without making any choice from a coarse moduli point.

proof.text: Fix $F/k$ and $C/F$ as in the statement. Regard $C$ as the corresponding map $c:\operatorname{Spec}F\to\mathcal M_{g,0}$. The normalization theorem identifies the restriction of $Z_{g,\ell}$ to $\mathcal M_{g,0}$ with the original full level scheme $L_{g,\ell}$, as a 2-cartesian square. Consequently the 2-fibre over $c$ has, on an $F$-scheme $B$, precisely pairs $(z,\beta)$ from the question: the second map to $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is its fixed structure map and the 2-isomorphism is the actual family isomorphism $\beta:a(z)\simeq C_B$. Both scheme functors are discrete, so an arrow between two such pairs forces $z=z^{\prime}$ and $\beta=\beta^{\prime}$. Restricting the 2-cartesian square to $c$ identifies this discrete functor with $\operatorname{Spec}F\times_{\mathcal M_{g,0}}L_{g,\ell}$: with this ordering the comparison is $C_B\to a(z)$, so use $\beta^{-1}$. Inverting again recovers $\beta$, and inversion commutes with pullback. The rigidification theorem identifies the latter, naturally in all $B$, with the full frame functor of $\mathcal H_{C_B/B}$. Concretely, a level frame on the family representing $z$ is sent to the frame on $C_B$ obtained by applying the inverse of $\beta^*$; the inverse construction equips $C_B$ with the given frame and uses the representing equivalence for $L_{g,\ell}$. The identity of these two operations follows from the frame-preserving isomorphism condition in the definition. The rigidification theorem also represents this frame functor by a finite etale surjective $F$-scheme. This proves the claimed natural isomorphism and representability. Surjectivity means the geometric fibres are nonempty; it does not require an $F$-rational frame.
